fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests - Bloomberg.com
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests. ## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AISubscribe. What started as a satirical online movement two months ago has turned into one of India’s biggest student protests in years, sparking scenes of violent clashes in New Delhi. And Prime Minister Narendra Modi has few good options to stop them. Launched in May by young organizers with little political experience, the Cockroach Janta Party managed to draw crowds of students, parents and professionals into the heart of India’s capital, where they jumped police barricades and faced tear gas and baton charges in an attempt to march to the parliament on Monday. They started by demanding the resignation of India’s education minister after a series of exam scandals, but frustrations quickly morphed into broader anger at Modi’s government. fusion_ranked_evidence.title: How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi - DW.com
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi. What started as a satirical protest against exam leaks in India has grown into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education. Riot police fired tear gas and used batons in New Delhi as tens of thousands of supporters of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) marched towards India's Parliament on Monday (July 20). The CJP began as an online campaign in May and rapidly evolved into a Gen Z street movement, giving a voice to a generation frustrated by unemployment, shrinking opportunities and a failing education system. The youth-led "Cockroach" party is now posing an unexpected challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, prompting a response that combines political outreach with police action. This is a worthless government," Renuka Chowdhury, an MP from India's opposition Congress party, told DW. The CJP movement gained fresh momentum over the weekend after veteran reform activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose three-week hunger strike has become a symbol of the protests, was forcibly taken to a hospital by police.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.

fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office. NEW DELHI — Supporters of India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement were caned by police Monday as they sought to march on parliament in the capital, New Delhi, despite authorities denying permission for the protest. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office, drawing millions of supporters on social media before broadening its appeal. A police decision to forcibly move hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital on Saturday has galvanized the movement, with thousands of supporters arriving through the night at the protest site of Jantar Mantar in the heart of New Delhi for the march on the opening day of parliament’s monsoon session.

fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'Cockroach' protests take on Modi with unlikely weapons: Sharp, irreverent humor and memes. NEW DELHI (AP) — India's young protesters are mocking their government. And the jokes are landing. As thousands of demonstrators take to the streets in the Indian capital, they are waging a parallel campaign online, flooding social media with memes, parody videos and self-deprecating jokes. In doing so, they are also beating Narendra Modi — the powerful but image-conscious prime minister — at his own game. Now protesters are using that same platform to mock his administration, ridicule pro-government television news coverage, transform confrontation with police into viral content and seize control of the online narrative. The campaign has taken the protests demanding accountability and education reforms beyond the streets, broadening its reach and intensifying pressure on a government wary of appearing to yield to a rapidly growing youth movement. fusion_ranked_evidence.title: CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi: The meme language of India's Gen Z 'cockroach' protest - BBC
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: On Monday, 20-year-old Chhavi (name changed) paused outside a Delhi metro station on her way to what would become one of the largest anti-government demonstrations against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government in the Indian capital in recent years. She balanced her phone against a railing, stepped back and filmed a quick "fit check" - a video showing off her outfit before the protest. Hours later, police fired tear gas and charged demonstrators with batons as tens of thousands of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) – a youth-led movement that grew from protests over exam irregularities into a broader campaign for government accountability – marched towards parliament. By evening, protesters said scores had been beaten by police, while police said several officers had also been injured. And when they turned to humour, it was almost always self-directed: joking about the kilometres logged fleeing baton charges or the absurdity of filming an outfit reveal moments before running into tear gas.
